Prevention: Rotate tobacco with non- solanaceous crops like maize, groundnuts in a 3-4 year rotation
Weed early in tobacco fields to remove alternate hosts which harbour budworms
Uproot and burn tobacco stalks soon after reaping at the end of the season (observe timely closed season)
Remove all plant residues/trash from the field which might harbour overwintering of pests
Currently there are no resistant tobacco varieties to budworms
Monitoring: First instar larvae are black, Older larvae are green to black, 3-4cm in length
A dirty white stripe with distinct spiracles(breathing holes) runs along each side
Appear at any time in the season
Attracted to young leaves at the bud
Budworms feed and chew buds and young leaves of tobacco plants
Check for holes on leaves, leads to tattered leaves
Apply control measures when the pest is seen
Direct Control: Hand pick budworms and destroy them
Uproot and burn all tobacco stalks to kill budworm overwintering insects
